text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the people are safe.

Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, and do not turn your backs on one another. O servants of Allah, be brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to stay angry with his brother for more than three days.

Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A person keeps telling the truth until they are recorded with Allah as truthful. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to Hell. A person keeps telling lies until they are recorded with Allah as a liar.
Do not argue with your brother, do not make jokes with him that he dislikes, and do not make him a promise that you will not keep.

Smiling in the face of your brother is charity. Enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity. Giving directions to a person who is lost is charity. Removing stones, thorns, or bones from the road is charity for you.
Actions are but by intentions, and every man shall have only that which he intended.
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
He who believes in Allah and the Last Day should either speak good or remain silent.
The best among you are those who have the best manners and character.
Allah does not look at your appearances or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your actions.
A person is with those whom he loves.
Whoever follows a path in pursuit of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise.
The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those that are most consistent, even if they are small.
Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
He who does not show mercy to our young and does not recognize the rights of our elders is not one of us.
Seven types of people will be shaded by Allah under His shade on the Day when there is no shade except His, including a person whose heart is attached to the mosques.
The upper hand is better than the lower hand.
Every religion has a character, and the character of Islam is modesty.
source: Ibn Majah, Zuhd, 17; Muwatta, Husn al-Khuluq, 9.

text: Wealth is not having many possessions; rather, true wealth is the richness of the soul.
A believer is not stung from the same hole twice.
The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever.
He is not a believer who eats his fill while his neighbor next to him goes hungry.
The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is trusted, he betrays.
Cleanliness is half of faith.
The most perfect of believers in faith are those who are best in character.
Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveler.
A strong person is not the one who can wrestle; the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry.
The one who points the way to good is like the one who does it.
Allah is Kind and He loves kindness in all matters.
Paradise lies under the feet of mothers.
The best of you is the one who is best to his family.
Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving alone that which does not concern him.
Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on the earth and the One in the heavens will have mercy upon you.
Avoid the seven great destructive sins: associating partners with Allah, magic, killing a soul, and the rest of the major destructive sins mentioned by the Prophet.
Pay the worker his wages before his sweat dries.
Religion is sincerity.
Fear Allah wherever you are, and follow up a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out.
He who cheats us is not one of us.
Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which wavers in your heart and which you do not want people to know about.
